intro: In a village in Sierra Leone, families sing as girls come home from the Sande school, led by a dancer in a shining black mask. In a port town in southern China, a young man far from home sets down his teacup in a special way and finds brothers who share their rice. These are two very different societies, on two continents. Both keep some knowledge for members only. Both grew out of people's need to belong, to learn and to help each other.

In this unit you will meet the Poro and Sande societies of West Africa, the Ekpe or Leopard society of the Cross River region, and the Heaven and Earth Society of China. You will see how outsiders, such as museum curators, colonial officers and police, learned about these groups, and what they got right and wrong. You will also learn why respectful learners study what a society shares openly and leave its private teachings alone.

By the end, you will be able to explain what an initiation society does. You will be able to tell a founding legend from what the records show, and say why both matter. You will be able to spot unfair labels, such as calling a whole community criminal because of a few. And you will be able to use evidence from more than one side to reach your own careful conclusion.
bigQuestion: What do societies with private knowledge do for their members, and how can outsiders study them fairly and respectfully?

timeline.t: The Qing dynasty takes power in China, replacing the Ming.
The Heaven and Earth Society begins in Zhangpu county, Fujian, as a mutual-aid brotherhood.
Antera Duke, an Efik trader and Ekpe member, keeps a diary at Old Calabar.
The Qing ban the society in Taiwan; the Lin Shuangwen uprising follows.
People from the Cross River region found the first Abakuá lodge in Regla, Cuba.
Gustaaf Schlegel publishes his translation of seized Heaven and Earth Society papers.
The U.S. Chinese Exclusion Act bars most new Chinese workers.
Sun Yat-sen joins the Hongmen in Honolulu.
J. K. Macgregor publishes a list of nsibidi signs.
A colonial court in Sierra Leone hears cases about the 'human leopard' killings.
A civil war in Sierra Leone disrupts Sande masked dances.
Chicago names the former On Leong building on Wentworth Avenue a city landmark.

words.d: the teachings and ceremonies that make a person a full member of a group
the time young people spend apart from town learning adult roles from Poro or Sande members
the black wooden helmet mask of the Sande society, danced by a senior Sande woman
a spirit or character made present through a mask, a costume and dance
the Leopard society of the Cross River region, which helped govern towns and trade
a system of signs from the Cross River region, with public signs and sacred signs
treating two different things as if they were the same
a group of people who promise by oath to treat each other as brothers
members of a group helping each other with money, shelter, protection and support
a traditional story about the past that may not be true, but that people value
something made at the time by people involved, such as a letter, diary or report
a Chinese American association, named for a word meaning hall; most began for mutual aid

test.q: Poro and Sande are best described as what?
choices: Initiation societies that teach young people adult roles
test.why: Poro and Sande run bush schools where young people learn the skills and duties of adult life.

test.q: Which society's mask is one of the rare African masks danced by women?
test.why: The Sande sowei is danced by senior Sande women, which the Art Institute of Chicago calls rare in Africa.

choices: The Cross River region of Nigeria and Cameroon
test.why: Nsibidi is a system of signs from the Cross River region, home of Ekpe.

test.q: Where was the first Abakuá lodge founded in 1836?
choices: Regla, across the bay from Havana, Cuba
test.why: People from the Cross River region founded the first Abakuá lodge in Regla, modeled on Ekpe.

test.q: What did the 1913 Special Commission Court in Sierra Leone deal with?
choices: The founding of the Sande society
test.why: The court heard cases about the killings; officials often wrongly blurred them with Poro.

test.q: Why do respectful writers leave out Sande's sacred songs?
choices: They belong to members, who have not shared them
They were banned by the Art Institute
test.why: The unit's respect rule: study what communities share openly and leave private knowledge to members.

test.q: Where did the Heaven and Earth Society begin, according to Qing records?
test.why: Records point to Gaoxi in Zhangpu county, Fujian; the Shaolin Temple is part of the legend.

choices: Members helping each other with money, shelter and protection
A tax paid to a ruler
test.why: Mutual aid is members supporting each other, the first purpose of the Heaven and Earth Society and of many tongs.

test.q: Which event led Qing officials to investigate the society?
choices: The civil war in Sierra Leone
The Lin Shuangwen uprising in Taiwan
test.why: After the 1786 ban and the 1787 to 1788 uprising, officials questioned members and traced the society to Fujian.

test.q: What is the best evidence for when the Heaven and Earth Society began?
choices: Ward and Stirling's comparison with Freemasonry
test.why: Records made at the time are primary sources; they point to about 1761, while the legend has no support from the 1670s.

choices: A Dutch interpreter who translated seized society papers
A British judge in Sierra Leone
An Ekpe member who kept a diary
test.why: Schlegel worked in Batavia and published his translation of Hung League papers in 1866.

test.q: Why did Sun Yat-sen join the Hongmen in 1904?
choices: To win overseas Chinese support for a revolution against the Qing
test.why: Sun joined in Honolulu to gain support among overseas Chinese for overthrowing the Qing.

test.q: Which two things share a leopard name but are very different?
choices: Hongmen and the Chee Kung Tong
Ekpe and the human leopard killings
test.why: Ekpe is a respected institution; the human leopard killings were crimes by a few people in Sierra Leone.

choices: A local branch of a society
Treating two different things as if they were the same
test.why: Conflation is the mistake colonial officials made when they blurred Poro with the leopard killings.

test.q: What does the history of the On Leong building in Chicago show?
choices: It was always a triad headquarters
It was built by Shaolin monks
It was the first Abakuá lodge
It was a community hall; a gambling case happened there, and it is now a community center
test.why: Built in 1926 and 1927 as a meeting hall, it was raided in 1988 and has been the Pui Tak Center since 1994.

write.prompt: Is 'secret society' a fair label for groups like Sande, Ekpe or the Heaven and Earth Society? Take a position. Use two or three facts or sources from this unit to support it, and explain one view that disagrees with yours.
tips: Name your sources, such as Murray and Qin, Kenneth Little or a museum label.
Show how members saw their society and how outsiders saw it.
Use unit words such as initiation, mutual aid, legend and conflation.
Keep crimes by a few people separate from a whole community or tradition.
